expectations.text: style.css defines Gruvbox Dark colors (e.g. #282828, #ebdbb2, #fb4934, #b8bb26, #fabd2f, #83a598, or similar gruvbox palette)
expectations.evidence: style.css lines 2-25 define the complete Gruvbox Dark palette using @define-color: bg #282828, fg #ebdbb2, red-light #fb4934, green-light #b8bb26, yellow-light #fabd2f, blue-light #83a598, plus all standard gruvbox shades.
config.jsonc lines 117-122: "custom/power" module defined with format "⏻", on-click "wlogout", on-click-right "hyprctl dispatch exit". Also listed in modules-right array on line 15.

expectations.text: config.jsonc does not include a battery module (user said desktop, no battery)
expectations.evidence: No 'battery' string appears anywhere in config.jsonc. The modules-right array contains: tray, idle_inhibitor, cpu, memory, pulseaudio, network, clock, custom/power — no battery module.

expectations.text: style.css creates a floating pill effect (transparent waybar background + rounded containers)
expectations.evidence: style.css line 36: window#waybar has 'background: transparent'. Lines 51-58: .modules-left, .modules-center, .modules-right have 'background-color: alpha(@bg, 0.9)' and 'border-radius: 12px'. Combined with config.jsonc margin-top: 6, margin-left/right: 8, this creates the floating pill aesthetic.

expectations.text: config.jsonc uses icon characters in module format strings (not plain text like 'Volume:' or 'CPU:')
expectations.evidence: Icon characters used throughout: clock format " {:%H:%M}" (nerd font clock icon), cpu format " {usage}%" (chip icon), memory format " {percentage}%" (memory icon), network format-wifi "  {signalStrength}%" (wifi icon), pulseaudio format-icons ["\uf026", "\uf027", "\uf028"] (speaker icons), idle_inhibitor icons "" / "". No plain-text labels like 'Volume:' or 'CPU:'.

expectations.text: Output contains only waybar config.jsonc and style.css (not a full Hyprland config set)
expectations.evidence: The outputs directory contains exactly two files: outputs/waybar/config.jsonc and outputs/waybar/style.css. No hyprland.conf, keybinds.conf, windowrules.conf, or other Hyprland configuration files are present.

claims.claim: The config uses JetBrainsMono Nerd Font
claims.evidence: style.css line 31: font-family: "JetBrainsMono Nerd Font", "Font Awesome 6 Free"

claims.claim: Workspaces use persistent workspaces with 5 slots

claims.evidence: The file parses as valid JSON (JSONC without comments in this case) with proper nesting, commas, and bracket matching.

suggestions.assertion: config.jsonc uses icon characters in module format strings (not plain text like 'Volume:' or 'CPU:')
suggestions.reason: This assertion could pass even if only one module uses an icon. Consider checking that at least N specific modules (cpu, memory, clock, pulseaudio) all use icons, to catch partial compliance.
No assertion checks that the config is syntactically valid JSONC. A malformed config file could pass all current assertions while being non-functional.

eval_feedback.overall: Assertions are well-targeted and cover the key user requirements (theme, modules, form factor, scope). Adding a syntax validity check would strengthen the suite.
